title: That's Bubble Gum - That's Giorgio
scene: 1960s German-language market / Hansa bubblegum and schlager
notes: Covers-heavy early bubblegum album with bright hooks, guitars and pre-disco arrangements.

title: Giorgio
scene: European bubblegum / Hansa-era pop and rock
notes: Reconfigured debut material with Moody Trudy and Arizona Man; not a fully distinct recording programme.

title: Son of My Father
scene: Early-1970s Munich pop studio / pre-disco synth experiments
notes: Moog and phased pop-rock point toward his electronic future; mostly live-band arrangements.

title: Giorgio's Music
scene: West German schlager and pop-rock / Philips
notes: German-language originals, melodic schlager and pop-rock; detailed production and mood evidence remains scarce.

title: Spinach 1
scene: West German rock-and-roll/pop; Spinach collaborative project
notes: Early Holm collaboration assembling singles-era rock and pop with unevenly documented synth elements.

title: Einzelgänger
notes: Sparse modular synth patterns, robotic vocal fragments and drones predate his disco breakthrough.

title: Knights in White Satin
notes: Lush Munich disco suite transforms a rock ballad with live strings and suggestive vocals.

title: From Here to Eternity
scene: Munich electronic disco / Oasis and Casablanca
notes: Seamlessly sequenced synthetic disco and vocoder harmonies anticipate electronic club music.

title: Love's in You, Love's in Me
scene: Munich disco / Casablanca-Oasis; Giorgio & Chris collaboration
notes: Chris Bennett-led romantic disco balances gentle vocals, live players, synthesizers and connected dance tracks.

title: Midnight Express
scene: 1978 electronic film score / Munich and Los Angeles sessions
notes: A sinister electronic film score mixing sequencer-driven Chase with ambient suspense and two vocal cuts.

title: Music From "Battlestar Galactica" and Other Original Compositions
scene: Munich space-disco / TV-theme reinterpretations and independent original composition
notes: Television themes reworked as disco; original fifteen-minute Evolution explores psychedelic synthetic grooves.

title: E=MC²
scene: Munich electronic disco / Soundstream live-to-digital production
notes: Bright digital-era disco marries synthesizers, programmed piano mechanisms, live drumming and Moroder vocoders.

title: American Gigolo
scene: Los Angeles electronic film scoring / disco and new-wave crossover
notes: Nocturnal synthesizer score surrounds Blondie’s rock-disco theme and a Mozart adaptation.

title: Foxes
scene: Casablanca disco-pop / Los Angeles movie soundtrack and hard-rock crossover
notes: Double-LP blend of disco vocals, atmospheric instrumentals and Angel’s guitar-driven rock.

title: Cat People
scene: Early-1980s electronic horror / erotic-thriller film scoring
notes: Ominous synthesizer cues, reversed tapes and Bowie’s commanding title performance dominate.

title: Solitary Men
scene: 1980s Munich/Los Angeles synth-led AOR and dance-pop collaboration
notes: Joe Esposito’s husky vocals bridge polished soft-rock ballads and synth-driven dance arrangements.
